Travel across Mongolia,
unhurried and well looked after.
hero.text: We have been running tours to every region of Mongolia since 2011, with guides and drivers who know the country well.

specialOffer.title: Golden Eagle Festival
specialOffer.text: A look at western Mongolian culture and customs. A few places remain for October.

intro.heading: A local team that knows Mongolia well.
paragraphs: Travels in Mongolia is a tour operator based in Ulaanbaatar. We run tours that share Mongolia's culture, history and landscape with visitors, and we try to do it in a way that is kind to the places we visit.
The company was founded by Doljmaa Songorov, who has worked in Mongolian tourism for many years. We keep groups small and take care of the logistics, so you can enjoy the trip.

toursSection.heading: Find a trip that suits you.

eventsBand.heading: Naadam, the Golden Eagle Festival and other traditions
eventsBand.text: If you can, plan your trip around one of Mongolia's festivals. We reserve places on the most popular departures each year.

testimonials.quote: We had a great time traveling around the Gobi. The driver was skilled and friendly, the guide knowledgeable and fluent. Every stop was different and worth the drive. We'd recommend Travels in Mongolia to anyone looking for an adventure.

testimonials.quote: Very professional throughout our 7-day Central Mongolia tour. Horse riding, camel riding, visiting nomadic families: we won't forget it. We'd happily recommend them.

testimonials.quote: From the first email to the last goodbye, everything ran smoothly. The small group and time with local families made it feel personal rather than packaged.

aboutPage.metaDescription: A local, independent tour operator in Mongolia, focused on sustainable tourism since 2011.

hero.heading: A local tour operator, run with care.

story.heading: Local roots, built up over time.
paragraphs: Travels in Mongolia is a local tour operator. Since 2011 we have worked directly with the herding families, camp owners, drivers and guides who make each trip possible.
We want to grow tourism that lasts, look after our guests, and share Mongolia's culture, history and landscape with travelers who care about them.

founder.name: Doljmaa Songorov
founder.text: Doljmaa has worked in Mongolian tourism for many years. She organizes the tours herself and keeps an eye on the details. Her contacts across the country help us arrange trips that feel relaxed and personal.
founder.quote: We'd like to introduce you to Mongolia the way we know it.

hero.text: Each itinerary is a starting point, and we can adjust the pace, comfort and route to suit you. Prices are per person for a private tour.

groupDeparturesPage.metaDescription: Join a small group on a set date, timed around Mongolia's festivals and best seasons.

hero.heading: Travel with a small group.
hero.text: We run a few set departures each year, timed around Mongolia's festivals and best seasons. Groups are limited to eight guests.

how.title: Departures go ahead
how.text: Once a date is listed, it runs. We don't cancel at the last minute for low numbers.

how.title: Maximum eight guests
how.text: Small enough to stay with nomadic families and keep things personal.

how.title: Festival places
how.text: We reserve seats and homestays at the busiest events.

travelToolsPage.metaDescription: What to know before you go: visas, timing, packing, health, money and staying connected in Mongolia.

essentials.label: Documents
essentials.title: Visas & entry
essentials.text: Many nationalities enter visa-free for up to 30 days; we'll check what applies to you and provide any invitation letters you need.

essentials.label: Timing
essentials.title: When to travel
essentials.text: June to September brings green steppe and warm days. October is eagle-festival season. Winter travel is possible if you don't mind the cold.

essentials.label: Packing
essentials.title: What to bring
essentials.text: Layers for wide temperature swings, sturdy footwear, sun protection and a good camera. We send a full packing list when you book.

essentials.label: Health
essentials.title: Staying well
essentials.text: No mandatory vaccinations, but routine ones should be current. We carry first-aid kits and a satellite phone on remote routes.

essentials.label: Money
essentials.title: Currency & tipping
essentials.text: The local currency is the tögrög. Carry some cash for remote areas; cards work in Ulaanbaatar. Tipping is appreciated but not expected.

essentials.label: Connectivity
essentials.title: Staying in touch
essentials.text: Mobile coverage is good near towns and patchy elsewhere. Remote trips carry a satellite phone.

faqs.question: How far in advance should I book?
faqs.answer: For festival departures and peak summer we recommend six to nine months. Tailored private trips can often be arranged with less notice — get in touch and we'll tell you what's realistic.

faqs.question: Are your trips private or group?
faqs.answer: Both. Most journeys are run privately just for you, at your own pace. We also offer a limited number of small-group departures each year on fixed dates.

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like?
faqs.answer: A mix of comfortable hotels in Ulaanbaatar and authentic tourist ger camps in the countryside — traditional felt tents with proper beds, and shared or private facilities depending on the camp.

faqs.question: Is Mongolia suitable for families or older travelers?
faqs.answer: Yes. We adjust the pace, driving distances and activities to your group. Tell us who is traveling and we'll plan around them.

faqs.question: How do payments and deposits work?
faqs.answer: A deposit secures your dates, with the balance due before travel. We'll send the terms in writing before anything is confirmed.

faqs.question: Can you arrange flights within Mongolia?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many itineraries include domestic flights to the Gobi, west and north, and we book them for you.
